newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IBM Hungary starts HUF 5 bln BCU service.
newsitem.headline: IBM Hungary starts HUF 5 bln BCU service.

text.p: IBM 's Hungarian unit launched a five-billion-forint pilot project aimed at providing low-cost computing solutions to businesses, a company official said on Thursday.
"Hungary is the first European country where we are introducing this service," Ferenc Bati, IBM Hungary's director in charge of the service, told Reuters.
The business computing utility (BCU) provides a comprehensive package of business applications for firms that need up-to-date business software but have limited free capital and manpower, he said.

In the initial stage, the servers will be running Libra, a business applications package developed by Hungary's Mikro Volan Elektronika, but plans include offering Lotus Notes and electronic data exchange (EDI), Bati said.
The service is available via leased lines or ISDN telephone lines and will be generally available in Hungary in the second half of 1997, once the tests have been completed.
"We have chosen Hungary for the European pilot service because of its dynamic growth, suitable network infrastructure and proper regulatory environment," IBM said in a statement.
